newsitem.title: UK: Euro bourses hit peaks on intrest rate hopes.
newsitem.headline: Euro bourses hit peaks on intrest rate hopes.

text.p: Major European bourses surged to hit new highs on Wednesday, lifted by a stronger dollar and a growing conviction that interest rates would remain steady.

On foreign exchanges, the dollar strengthened to a new four-year high against the yen and gained against the mark, its long-standing buoyancy overcoming bullish mark sentiment sparked by new tensions over Europe's single currency.

In London, stocks soared to a trading record of 4286.9 points on the FTSE index, beating the previous best set only yesterday, and hovered just below that after the Bank of England signalled no change in interest rates.
Few had anticipated a rate hike, but the risk of a surprise kept the market on edge, dealers said.

Traders were still waiting for the outcome of a session of the U.S. central bank's policy-making committee on interest rates in the influential U.S. economy. The Federal Open Markets committee makes its announcement at 1915 GMT tonight though no change in monetary policy is expected in the U.S. either.

Recent economic statistics in the U.S. continue to show non-inflationary growth whilst in Britain economists expect finance minister Kenneth Clarke to continue to resist rate rises at such a politically-sensitive time. The British government has to call a general election by late May.
But meanwhile, Wall Street made a good start on Wednesday, climbing 0.35 percent, further cheering European bourses.
Yet some investors remained on edge ahead of London's reporting season as some companies have been hit by the appreciation in sterling on the foreign exchange markets.
"The (price/earnings) ratings in this market are very demanding and we really do need to see the proof that the market's optimism is merited by the results," said a trader.
In Frankfurt, floor trading closed at a new peak of 3098.0 on the DAX index boosted by the strength of the dollar trading above 1.64 marks, which was soon as boosted export prospects.

"There is strong support there from the dollar and the focus is very much on individual stocks, although the chemical sector is strong because of the dollar. The specific interest this morning is on Lufthansa ," said one trader.
In Paris, French stocks also rose to new highs on expectations the U.S. central bank would not raise interest rates after the Federal Open Market Committee meeting, brokers said.
"There's a feeling that the Fed will hold still for the time being," a trader said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index, bolstered by a strong dollar and rising bond prices, was up 1.53 percent, at 2,544.06 before falling back slightly in afternoon trading.

On currency markets, the dollar, at a four-year high against the yen, was seen as retaining its strong tone but was unlikely to jump in either direction as the market awaited the results of the FOMC meeting.
"The dollar's looking well bid, particularly against the yen...but for now people are just waiting to get the FOMC out of the way," said one trader at a U.S. bank in London.

The dollar was at 123.30 yen in afternoon deals, just off its fresh four-year high of 123.35 but well above its late Tuesday European level of 122.30. Against the mark, it was at 1.6477 compared with 1.6424 on Tuesday.

The mark got a boost earlier from a Financial Times report that Italy would be offered a compromise deal to delay its entry into EMU until 2000 or 2001. An EU official said such a plan was being considered "in some quarters".
"Initially, dollar/mark was depressed today because there was a lot of mark buying against the lira on the news about EMU," the bank trader said.

"It's the contrast between very strong growth in the U.S. and weak growth in Japan and Europe that is driving the dollar higher, and there's nothing on the horizon that's going to change that," said Keith Edmonds, chief analyst at IBJ International in London.
A 1.4 percent drop in December German industrial orders, announced earlier, provided new evidence of a sluggish German economy.
In European currencies, the pound was buoyant, led by heavy buying against the yen overnight which had pushed sterling/yen to a 52-month high.
Sterling hit a 52-month high of 201.26 yen at 1240 GMT in early afternoon, up from 198.55 seen late on Tuesday.
CURRENCIES AT 1500 GMT
The dollar was at 1.6477 marks and 123.30 yen after closing in Europe at 1.6424 marks and 122.30 yen on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1500 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was 19.5 points higher at 4,280.4.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed 30.94 points higher at 3,098.00.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 36.97 at 2,540.7.
PRECIOUS METALS - Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $343.40 an ounce after closing in Europe on Tuesday at $346.30.
